# Data samples: central-banks

Every data type of `central-banks` as a real record of the committed test data, every field explained from its data contract, the fields only other rows have and a checklist for the production query. The [index](README.md) lists every domain.

- [central-bank](#central-bank)
- [rate-series](#rate-series)

<a id="central-bank"></a>

## Central bank: central-bank (CBANK)

One central bank: its policy rate, the last move, the rate's history and the market series around it. One row per central bank, keyed by BANK_ID. Read by the **central-banks** pack's connector `centralbank-store` (lake table `centralbank.central-bank`). There is **no committed test data** for this kind: the sample comes from the pack's samples (`config/packs/economy/central-banks/samples/central-bank.jsonl`, 2 records). A bank or a public refresh delivers it in the same JSON Lines shape.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `config/packs/economy/central-banks/samples/central-bank.jsonl` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line |
| Key field | `BANK_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the pack's samples are served on every business date (partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | `NAME`, `COUNTRY`, `POLICY_RATE`, `POLICY_RATE_DATE`, `LAST_MOVE_DATE`, `LAST_MOVE_BP` |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | no committed files |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 2 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json
{
  "BANK_ID": "CBANK-BOC",
  "COUNTRY": "CAN",
  "COUNTRY_NAME": "Canada",
  "CURRENCY": "CAD",
  "LAST_MOVE_BP": 25.0,
  "LAST_MOVE_DATE": "2026-10-29",
  "NAME": "Bank of Canada",
  "POLICY_HISTORY": [
    {
      "DATE": "2025-10-02",
      "VALUE": 2.5
    },
    {
      "DATE": "2025-10-03",
      "VALUE": 2.5
    },
    "… 280 more elements of the same shape"
  ],
  "POLICY_RATE": 2.5,
  "POLICY_RATE_DATE": "2026-11-05",
  "POLICY_SERIES": "CBSER-BOC-V39079",
  "PRESS": "PRESS-BOC",
  "PROVENANCE": {
    "ATTRIBUTION": "Source: Bank of Canada.",
    "DATASET": "Bank of Canada: policy rate and market series",
    "INTERNAL_ONLY": false,
    "LICENCE": "Bank of Canada terms of use: free to use, copy, distribute and transmit with attribution; inside a paid service, tell buyers the data is free on bankofcanada.ca",
    "RETRIEVED_AT": "2026-11-06",
    "SOURCE": "Bank of Canada",
    "URL": "https://www.bankofcanada.ca"
  },
  "SERIES": [
    {
      "CHANGE": 0.0,
      "DATE": "2026-11-05",
      "LATEST": 2.5,
      "RATE_SERIES": "CBSER-BOC-V39079",
      "TITLE": "Bank of Canada target for the overnight rate",
      "UNIT": "%"
    },
    {
      "CHANGE": 0.0,
      "DATE": "2026-11-05",
      "LATEST": 2.52,
      "RATE_SERIES": "CBSER-BOC-AVG_INTWO",
      "TITLE": "CORRA, Canadian overnight repo rate average",
      "UNIT": "%"
    },
    "… 3 more elements of the same shape"
  ],
  "WEBSITE": "https://www.bankofcanada.ca"
}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BANK_ID` | string | required | CBANK- and the bank's short id in the feed's YAML (FED, BOC). | pattern `^CBANK-` | `"CBANK-BOC"` |
| `COUNTRY` | string | required | The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the bank's country. | — | `"CAN"` |
| `COUNTRY_NAME` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The bank's country. | — | `"Canada"` |
| `CURRENCY` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The ISO 4217 code of the bank's currency. | — | `"CAD"` |
| `LAST_MOVE_BP` | number | optional (filled in every row) | The size of that move: the new rate less the old one, in basis points (negative for a cut). | unit: bp | `25.0` |
| `LAST_MOVE_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | optional (filled in every row) | The first date the policy rate took its current value, within the history window; empty when it did not move in the window. | — | `"2026-10-29"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The central bank's name. | — | `"Bank of Canada"` |
| `POLICY_HISTORY` | array of objects | required | The policy rate by date over the window, oldest first (DATE, VALUE). | — | [282 objects] |
| `POLICY_HISTORY[].DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The observation's date (a monthly series is dated the first of its month). | — | `"2025-10-02"` |
| `POLICY_HISTORY[].VALUE` | number | required | The observation, in the series' unit. | unit: the record's UNIT | `2.5` |
| `POLICY_RATE` | number | optional (filled in every row) | The latest value of the bank's policy-rate series (the Fed: the target range's upper limit; the Bank of Canada: the target for the overnight rate). | unit: % | `2.5` |
| `POLICY_RATE_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | optional (filled in every row) | The date of that value. | — | `"2026-11-05"` |
| `POLICY_SERIES` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The rate-series page of the policy rate. | pattern `^CBSER-`; links to `rate-series` | `"CBSER-BOC-V39079"` |
| `PRESS` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The bank's publisher page in the official-news pack (PRESS-<id>). | pattern `^PRESS-`; links to `release-source` | `"PRESS-BOC"` |
| `PROVENANCE` | object | required | Where the record comes from, one object: SOURCE, DATASET, RETRIEVED_AT, LICENCE, ATTRIBUTION, URL and INTERNAL_ONLY. | — | {…} |
| `PROVENANCE.ATTRIBUTION` | string | required | The credit line to repeat when the data is shown or republished. | — | `"Source: Bank of Canada."` |
| `PROVENANCE.DATASET` | string | required | The source and the series (or the bank) the record was built from. | — | `"Bank of Canada: policy rate and market series"` |
| `PROVENANCE.INTERNAL_ONLY` | boolean | required | True when the source's terms forbid redistribution outside the organisation (Export data refuses the record). | — | `false` |
| `PROVENANCE.LICENCE` | string | required | The terms under which the source allows reuse, as recorded in the feed's YAML. | — | `"Bank of Canada terms of use: free to use, copy, distribute…` |
| `PROVENANCE.RETRIEVED_AT` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The business date of the feed's pull that wrote the record. | — | `"2026-11-06"` |
| `PROVENANCE.SOURCE` | string | required | The organisation whose published data the record holds. | — | `"Bank of Canada"` |
| `PROVENANCE.URL` | string | required | The source's page for this record. | — | `"https://www.bankofcanada.ca"` |
| `SERIES` | array of objects | required | Every series of the bank the feed follows, one row each: RATE_SERIES, TITLE, LATEST, DATE, CHANGE, UNIT. | — | [5 objects] |
| `SERIES[].CHANGE` | number | optional (filled in every `SERIES[]` entry) | The latest value less the previous observation. | unit: the row's UNIT | `0.0` |
| `SERIES[].DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date of the latest value. | — | `"2026-11-05"` |
| `SERIES[].LATEST` | number | required | The series' latest value, in its unit. | unit: the row's UNIT | `2.5` |
| `SERIES[].RATE_SERIES` | string | required | The rate-series page (CBSER-<source>-<code>). | pattern `^CBSER-`; links to `rate-series` | `"CBSER-BOC-V39079"` |
| `SERIES[].TITLE` | string | required | The series' title in the feed's YAML. | — | `"Bank of Canada target for the overnight rate"` |
| `SERIES[].UNIT` | string | required | What the series measures. | seen: `%`, `CAD per USD`, `USD millions`, `index 1982-84=100, SA`, `percentage points` | `"%"` |
| `WEBSITE` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The bank's website. | — | `"https://www.bankofcanada.ca"` |

### Fields in other rows

None: all 2 rows were read, and every field any of them has is in the record above.

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `BANK_ID` per `snapshot`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `BANK_ID`, `NAME`, `COUNTRY`, `POLICY_HISTORY`, `SERIES`, `PROVENANCE` (the contract's required fields); every row of the test data also fills `COUNTRY_NAME`, `CURRENCY`, `LAST_MOVE_BP`, `LAST_MOVE_DATE`, `POLICY_RATE`, `POLICY_RATE_DATE`, `POLICY_SERIES`, `PRESS`, `WEBSITE`.
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Unique: `BANK_ID` per snapshot.
- `BANK_ID` matches `^CBANK-`.

<a id="rate-series"></a>

## Central bank series: rate-series (CBSER)

One central-bank or market series from FRED or the Bank of Canada: the history, the latest value, the change on the day and on the year. One row per central bank series, keyed by SERIES_ID. Read by the **central-banks** pack's connector `centralbank-store` (lake table `centralbank.rate-series`). There is **no committed test data** for this kind: the sample comes from the pack's samples (`config/packs/economy/central-banks/samples/rate-series.jsonl`, 13 records). A bank or a public refresh delivers it in the same JSON Lines shape.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `config/packs/economy/central-banks/samples/rate-series.jsonl` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line |
| Key field | `SERIES_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the pack's samples are served on every business date (partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | `SOURCE`, `CODE`, `CENTRAL_BANK`, `TITLE`, `UNIT`, `LATEST`, `LATEST_DATE`, `CHANGE` |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | no committed files |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 13 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json
{
  "CENTRAL_BANK": "CBANK-BOC",
  "CHANGE": 0.0,
  "CHANGE_1Y": 0.25,
  "CODE": "AVG.INTWO",
  "DESCRIPTION": "A measure of the cost of overnight general collateral funding in Canadian dollars using Government of Canada treasury bills and bonds as collateral for repurchase transactions (repos).",
  "FREQUENCY": "Business daily",
  "HIGH": 2.56,
  "HISTORY": [
    {
      "DATE": "2025-10-02",
      "VALUE": 2.56
    },
    {
      "DATE": "2025-10-03",
      "VALUE": 2.56
    },
    "… 271 more elements of the same shape"
  ],
  "LATEST": 2.52,
  "LATEST_DATE": "2026-11-05",
  "LOW": 2.24,
  "NAME": "CORRA, Canadian overnight repo rate average",
  "OBSERVATIONS": 273,
  "PREVIOUS": 2.52,
  "PREVIOUS_DATE": "2026-11-04",
  "PROVENANCE": {
    "ATTRIBUTION": "Source: Bank of Canada.",
    "DATASET": "Bank of Canada: AVG.INTWO",
    "INTERNAL_ONLY": false,
    "LICENCE": "Bank of Canada terms of use: free to use, copy, distribute and transmit with attribution; inside a paid service, tell buyers the data is free on bankofcanada.ca",
    "RETRIEVED_AT": "2026-11-06",
    "SOURCE": "Bank of Canada",
    "URL": "https://www.bankofcanada.ca/valet/series/AVG.INTWO"
  },
  "SERIES_ID": "CBSER-BOC-AVG_INTWO",
  "SOURCE": "Bank of Canada",
  "TITLE": "CORRA, Canadian overnight repo rate average",
  "UNIT": "%"
}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CENTRAL_BANK` | string | required | The central-bank page the series belongs to (CBANK-<id>). | pattern `^CBANK-`; links to `central-bank` | `"CBANK-BOC"` |
| `CHANGE` | number | optional (filled in every row) | The latest observation less the previous one, in the series' unit. | unit: the record's UNIT | `0.0` |
| `CHANGE_1Y` | number | optional (filled in 85% of rows) | The latest observation less the last one at least a year before it; empty when the window is shorter. | unit: the record's UNIT | `0.25` |
| `CODE` | string | required | The series' code at its source (DGS10, V39079). | — | `"AVG.INTWO"` |
| `DESCRIPTION` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The source's description of the series (FRED's notes, the Valet description), cut at 600 characters. | — | `"A measure of the cost of overnight general collateral fund…` |
| `FREQUENCY` | string | optional (filled in every row) | How often the source publishes the series, in its own words. | seen: `Business daily`, `Daily`, `Daily, 7-Day`, `Monthly`, `Weekly, As of Wednesday` | `"Business daily"` |
| `HIGH` | number | required | The highest observation in the history window. | unit: the record's UNIT | `2.56` |
| `HISTORY` | array of objects | required | The observations over the window (the feed's history-days), oldest first (DATE, VALUE). | — | [273 objects] |
| `HISTORY[].DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The observation's date (a monthly series is dated the first of its month). | — | `"2025-10-02"` |
| `HISTORY[].VALUE` | number | required | The observation, in the series' unit. | unit: the record's UNIT | `2.56` |
| `LATEST` | number | required | The latest observation, in the series' unit. | unit: the record's UNIT | `2.52` |
| `LATEST_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date of the latest observation. | — | `"2026-11-05"` |
| `LOW` | number | required | The lowest observation in the history window. | unit: the record's UNIT | `2.24` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The series' title, as NAME for search. | — | `"CORRA, Canadian overnight repo rate average"` |
| `OBSERVATIONS` | integer | required | How many observations the history holds. | — | `273` |
| `PREVIOUS` | number | optional (filled in every row) | The observation before the latest one. | unit: the record's UNIT | `2.52` |
| `PREVIOUS_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | optional (filled in every row) | The date of the previous observation. | — | `"2026-11-04"` |
| `PROVENANCE` | object | required | Where the record comes from, one object: SOURCE, DATASET, RETRIEVED_AT, LICENCE, ATTRIBUTION, URL and INTERNAL_ONLY. | — | {…} |
| `PROVENANCE.ATTRIBUTION` | string | required | The credit line to repeat when the data is shown or republished. | seen: `Source: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; the series' original source as FRED names it.`, `Source: Bank of Canada.` | `"Source: Bank of Canada."` |
| `PROVENANCE.DATASET` | string | required | The source and the series (or the bank) the record was built from. | — | `"Bank of Canada: AVG.INTWO"` |
| `PROVENANCE.INTERNAL_ONLY` | boolean | required | True when the source's terms forbid redistribution outside the organisation (Export data refuses the record). | — | `false` |
| `PROVENANCE.LICENCE` | string | required | The terms under which the source allows reuse, as recorded in the feed's YAML. | seen: `FRED API terms of use; each series keeps its owner's terms. The default series are US government works (Federal Reserve Board, US Treasury, BLS): public domain`, `Bank of Canada terms of use: free to use, copy, distribute and transmit with attribution; inside a paid service, tell buyers the data is free on bankofcanada.ca` | `"Bank of Canada terms of use: free to use, copy, distribute…` |
| `PROVENANCE.RETRIEVED_AT` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The business date of the feed's pull that wrote the record. | — | `"2026-11-06"` |
| `PROVENANCE.SOURCE` | string | required | The organisation whose published data the record holds. | seen: `FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis`, `Bank of Canada` | `"Bank of Canada"` |
| `PROVENANCE.URL` | string | required | The source's page for this record. | — | `"https://www.bankofcanada.ca/valet/series/AVG.INTWO"` |
| `SERIES_ID` | string | required | CBSER-, the source (FRED or BOC) and the source's series code with dots as underscores. | pattern `^CBSER-` | `"CBSER-BOC-AVG_INTWO"` |
| `SOURCE` | string | required | The source the series is read from: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis) or the Bank of Canada. | one of `Bank of Canada`, `FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis` | `"Bank of Canada"` |
| `TITLE` | string | required | The series' title in the feed's YAML, else the source's own. | — | `"CORRA, Canadian overnight repo rate average"` |
| `UNIT` | string | required | What the series measures (%, percentage points, an index, USD millions, CAD per USD). | seen: `%`, `CAD per USD`, `USD millions`, `index 1982-84=100, SA`, `percentage points` | `"%"` |

### Fields in other rows

None: all 13 rows were read, and every field any of them has is in the record above.

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `SERIES_ID` per `snapshot`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `SERIES_ID`, `NAME`, `SOURCE`, `CODE`, `CENTRAL_BANK`, `TITLE`, `UNIT`, `LATEST`, `LATEST_DATE`, `HIGH`, `LOW`, `OBSERVATIONS`, `HISTORY`, `PROVENANCE` (the contract's required fields); every row of the test data also fills `CHANGE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `FREQUENCY`, `PREVIOUS`, `PREVIOUS_DATE`.
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Unique: `SERIES_ID` per snapshot.
- `SERIES_ID` matches `^CBSER-`.
